(a) Title VII.—Section 741 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 293e) is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a)—
            (A) by striking the subsection heading and inserting “Cultural Competency, Prevention, and Public Health and Individuals With Disability Grants”; and 
            (B) in paragraph (1), by striking “for the purpose of” and all that follows through the period at the end and inserting “for the development, evaluation, and dissemination of research, demonstration projects, and model curricula for cultural competency, prevention, public health proficiency, reducing health disparities, and aptitude for working with individuals with disabilities training for use in health professions schools and continuing education programs, and for other purposes determined as appropriate by the Secretary.”; and  
        (2) by striking subsection (b) and inserting the following:“(b) Collaboration.—In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall collaborate with health professional societies, licensing and accreditation entities, health professions schools, and experts in minority health and cultural competency, prevention, and public health and disability groups, community-based organizations, and other organizations as determined appropriate by the Secretary. The Secretary shall coordinate with curricula and research and demonstration projects developed under section 807.“(c) Dissemination.—“(1) In general.—Model curricula developed under this section shall be disseminated through the Internet Clearinghouse under section 270 and such other means as determined appropriate by the Secretary.“(2) Evaluation.—The Secretary shall evaluate the adoption and the implementation of cultural competency, prevention, and public health, and working with individuals with a disability training curricula, and the facilitate inclusion of these competency measures in quality measurement systems as appropriate.“(d) Authorization of Appropriations.—There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section such sums as may be necessary for each of fiscal years 2010 through 2015.”.  
    (b) Title VIII.—Section 807 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 296e–1) is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a)—
            (A) by striking the subsection heading and inserting “Cultural Competency, Prevention, and Public Health and Individuals With Disability Grants”; and 
            (B) by striking “for the purpose of” and all that follows through “health care.” and inserting “for the development, 
evaluation, and dissemination of research, demonstration projects, and model curricula for cultural competency, prevention, public health proficiency, reducing health disparities, and aptitude for working with individuals with disabilities training for use in health professions schools and continuing education programs, and for other purposes determined as appropriate by the Secretary.”; and  
        (2) by redesignating subsection (b) as subsection (d); 
        (3) by inserting after subsection (a) the following:“(b) Collaboration.—In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall collaborate with the entities described in section 741(b). The Secretary shall coordinate with curricula and research and demonstration projects developed under such section 741.“(c) Dissemination.—Model curricula developed under this section shall be disseminated and evaluated in the same manner as model curricula developed under section 741, as described in subsection (c) of such section.”; and 
        (4) in subsection (d), as so redesignated—
            (A) by striking “subsection (a)” and inserting “this section”; and 
            (B) by striking “2001 through 2004” and inserting “2010 through 2015”.

fable.w: The section requires the Secretary to collaborate with non-federal parties (professional societies, accreditation entities, schools, outside experts, disability groups and community-based organizations) when carrying out the federal curricula and grant program. The tempting reading is that this is only a grant program, or only an amendment about curricula content, and so not participation. That reading fails because the collaboration mandate is a separate duty that brings outside entities into how the Secretary implements the program, which crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall collaborate with health professional societies, licensing and accreditation entities, health professions schools, and experts in minority health and cultural competency, prevention, and public health and disability groups, community-based organizations, and other organizations as determined appropriate by the Secretary.

qwen_block.w: The section explicitly requires the Secretary to collaborate with various outside entities, including health professional societies, experts, and community-based organizations, which are outside the federal government. This collaboration occurs in the context of carrying out the grant program, constituting participation as defined. The tempting reading might be that this is just administrative coordination, but the definition includes coordination with outside entities before or during a federal decision/action.
qwen_block.s: In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall collaborate with health professional societies, licensing and accreditation entities, health professions schools, and experts in minority health and cultural competency, prevention, and public health and disability groups, community-based organizations, and other organizations as determined appropriate by the Secretary.

opus.w: The Secretary must collaborate with non-federal entities (professional societies, accreditation bodies, schools, outside experts, disability groups, community-based organizations) while carrying out the federal program that develops and spreads model curricula. That is required coordination with outsiders on federal action. The tempting 'No' reading treats this as just a grant program or the content of a study, but these outside groups are not applicants. They are required collaborators in how the Secretary runs the program.
opus.s: (b) Collaboration.—In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall collaborate with health professional societies, licensing and accreditation entities, health professions schools, and experts in minority health and cultural competency, prevention, and public health and disability groups, community-based organizations, and other organizations as determined appropriate by the Secretary.
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **Yes**, with moderate confidence (about 0.72).

**The tempting "No" reading:** this is a grant program, and applying for grants is not participation. Example 3 also points that way: consulting outside experts on the content of a study was not counted as participation. But in this section the outside groups are not grant applicants. The law requires the Secretary to collaborate with them while running the program, including deciding how model curricula are developed, evaluated and spread.

**Why "Yes" holds:** the people the Secretary must work with are outside the federal government. They include professional societies, licensing and accreditation bodies, health professions schools, outside experts, disability groups and community-based organizations. That crosses the federal boundary. The section also requires coordination with projects under section 807, but that is coordination within the government and adds nothing. The remaining doubt is whether "carrying out" a grant program counts as a federal decision, or is closer to the study-content situation in Example 3.
